back: An all-night meeting with songs and speeches at which guerrillas won the support of villagers.
Fenced villages into which the Rhodesian government moved rural people to cut them off from guerrillas.
ZANLA attacked Altena Farm in the Centenary area, beginning the new phase of the war.

front: What did Mozambique do in March 1976?
back: It closed its border to Rhodesia and allowed ZANLA camps.

front: What were the Nyadzonia and Chimoio raids?
back: Rhodesian attacks on ZANLA camps in Mozambique in August 1976 and November 1977; death tolls are disputed.

front: When was the Patriotic Front formed?
back: October 1976, as an alliance between ZAPU and ZANU.

front: Why was the war more successful after 1972?
back: Villagers were prepared first, and Mozambique provided bases and a long border.

front: How did the war pressure Rhodesia by 1979?
back: Loss of control of the countryside, white emigration, sanctions and war costs, and pressure from neighbours and the West.

front: How many people died in the war?
back: Estimates range from about 20,000 to 30,000 or more; most were civilians; no exact figure is agreed.
